text: The PLOB bound caps the secret-key rate of any repeaterless QKD protocol at roughly 1.44 eta bits per channel use. At an attenuation of 0.2 dB/km, why does this make 1,000 km of direct transmission hopeless?
choices: Because polarization drift scrambles the key faster than it can be corrected
Because the no-cloning theorem forbids sending more than one bit per photon
Because 1,000 km exceeds the coherence length of any laser
Because eta is about 10^-20 at 1,000 km, so even a 10 GHz single-photon source delivers roughly one photon per three centuries
explanation: Loss is exponential — eta = 10^(-alpha L/10) reaches about 10^-20 at 1,000 km — so the surviving photon flux collapses to roughly one photon per three centuries, making direct QKD absurd and motivating repeaters and satellites. Choice 0 is a real but secondary engineering issue, not the PLOB wall; choice 1 misstates no-cloning; choice 2 confuses channel loss with laser coherence.
